overview: Global Initiative of Academic Networks (GIAN) is a Government of India program in Higher Education aimed at tapping the talent pool of scientists and entrepreneurs internationally to encourage their engagement with Indian higher education institutes, augment academic resources, accelerate quality reform, and elevate India's scientific and technological capacity to global excellence. It facilitates short to semester-long courses by foreign faculty in Indian institutions, promoting international academic collaboration and knowledge exchange.
objectives: Increase footfalls of reputed international faculty in Indian academic institutes
Provide opportunity for faculty to learn and share knowledge in cutting-edge areas
Provide opportunity for students to seek knowledge from international faculty
Create avenue for collaborative research with international faculty
Increase participation of international students in academic institutes
Enable interaction between students of different institutes in niche areas
Provide opportunity for technical persons from Indian industry to update knowledge
Motivate international experts to work on India-related problems
Develop high-quality course material in niche areas for wider use
Document and develop new pedagogic methods in emerging topics
eligibility: All Government (State or Central) higher education Institutions / University which are in top 200 in NIRF overall rankings and having at least NAAC ‘A’ grade (3.0 and above).
benefits: International faculty engagement, knowledge exchange, collaborative research opportunities, course development, pedagogic innovation, global exposure for students and faculty, access to international expertise, creation of digital repository for future viewing via National Digital Library, potential for MOOC creation, honorarium and travel support for foreign faculty, honorarium for host faculty and local coordinator, video recording and webcasting facilities, online feedback mechanism.
financial_support: A lump-sum amount of up to US$ 8000 for 12 to 14 hours of contact and up to US$ 12000 for 20 to 28 hours of contact can be paid to foreign experts covering travel and honorarium. Local hospitality is arranged by the Host Institute. The National Coordinator can spend Rs 1.0 crore for portal development and initial activities. Each Group Coordinator can spend Rs 50 lakhs from Plan grant for group activities. Funding for courses by Institutes is partially supported through Plan/Non-Plan Funds, TEQIP, UGC, AICTE, DST, DSIR, sponsorships, industry/foundations, participant fees, and other sources.
grant_amount_per_entity: Up to US$ 8000 for short duration courses (12-14 hours) and up to US$ 12000 for longer duration courses (20-28 hours) for foreign faculty honorarium and travel.
application_process: 1. Institute confirms eligibility (top 200 NIRF, NAAC A grade). 2. Competent authority appoints a local coordinator for GIAN. 3. Institute sends formal request letter from VC/Director, NAAC ‘A’ grade certificate, proof of NIRF ranking in top 200, and formal office order for local coordinator appointment (with name, email, mobile) to National Coordinator at IIT Kharagpur via email/speed post. 4. After document verification, Institute is added to GIAN program and login created for local coordinator. 5. Local coordinator logs into GIAN portal, edits profile, circulates proposal template to faculty. 6. Local coordinator invites course coordinators to submit proposals via portal. 7. Course coordinator uploads proposal in PDF format and submits. 8. Local coordinator scrutinizes proposal and foreign faculty consent form, then forwards to GIAN office by clicking ‘Accept’. 9. Proposal sent for document verification; if in order, forwarded to Chairman of appropriate sectional committee for review. 10. Status updates until approval by Apex body (GIAN Implementation Committee). 11. Upon approval, local coordinator receives mail to upload final brochure and course dates. 12. Local coordinator coordinates with course coordinator to upload brochure and finalize dates. 13. Official signed sanction letter with fund details sent to Institute. 14. Fund allocated released via PFMS after brochure upload. 15. During course, local coordinator monitors via portal, ensures participant feedback submission. 16. After course, local coordinator submits course completion report and fund utilization certificate to IIT Kharagpur within 15 days.
required_documents: Formal request letter from the highest Authority (VC / Director) of the Institute
Proof of NIRF Ranking in top 200
Formal office order for appointment of local coordinator, GIAN of the Institute/University (including name, email address and mobile number)
deadlines: Proposals may be submitted throughout the year. Three months required for review to final approval. Preferably, six months lead time from date of holding the course.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Education (formerly Ministry of Human Resource Development)
contact_details: Official Query Email: gian [at] iitkgp [dot] ac [dot] in | Phone: +91-3222-282288 | Profile Updating, Courses Registration & Participant Login Portal Email: gian [at] iitkgp [dot] ac [dot] in
caveats: Foreign faculty not entitled to travel allowance in virtual mode; only honorarium paid
Honorarium for foreign faculty in virtual mode limited to $3000 for one week course (≥12 hrs) and $5000 for 2 week course (≥20 hrs)
Contingencies and other expenses (excluding travel and honorarium of foreign faculty) should not exceed 35% of total fund provided for a course
A maximum of Rs. 5000/- per course may be earmarked to local coordinator for office expenses and honorarium from contingency expense
All approved courses must be completed by 31st December 2020 (per Local Coordinator manual, though this may be outdated)
Dollar conversion rate fixed at Rs. 83 for payment to host institute for F.Y. 2023-24, subject to review for subsequent years
GIAN to MOOC conversion of completed courses discontinued for both in-person and virtual mode
